# A tetrahedral cap variance bound at its actual section centroid

Let a plane meet the interior of a tetrahedron T. Let F in (0,1) be the fraction of volume on either chosen side, and let b=(b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3) be the barycentric centroid of the actual two-dimensional section. Then, for EVERY vertex index j,

    F(1-F) <= 27 product_(i!=j) b_i.                (1)

For a strict quadrilateral section, every inequality in (1) is strict. There is no centrality, optimizing-cut, or symmetry assumption. The constant 27 is sharp for proper sections through an edge. This is an ordinary tetrahedral geometric statement; no mixed-integer conclusion is inferred from it.

## 1. Strict quadrilaterals and a positive polynomial certificate

Label the chosen captured vertices 0,1 and use raw plane values (p,q,-r,-s), where p,q,r,s>0. Define

    D=pq(r+s)+rs(p+q),  theta=ps(q+r)/D.

The actual section-centroid formula is

    3b_0=r/(p+r)+theta s/(p+s),
    3b_1=s/(q+s)+(1-theta)r/(q+r),
    3b_2=p/(p+r)+(1-theta)q/(q+r),
    3b_3=q/(q+s)+theta p/(p+s).                     (2)

For example the four edge intersection points have supports 02,03,13,12. Splitting their quadrilateral into two triangles gives their area ratio theta and yields (2). These formulas, including their geometric derivation, also appear in `candidate 5c1f3bb21840ea60`.

The cap fraction has the positive-denominator formula

    F=[p^2q^2+pq(p+q)(r+s)+rs(p^2+pq+q^2)]
          /[(p+r)(p+s)(q+r)(q+s)].                 (3)

It follows either from tetrahedral triangulation or by canceling

    [p^3/((p+r)(p+s))-q^3/((q+r)(q+s))]/(p-q).

Formula (3) is valid also at p=q, and no equal-height case is discarded.

Put M_ab=r^a s^b+r^b s^a when a>b, and M_aa=r^a s^a. Define N(p,q,r,s)=sum C_ij(r,s)p^i q^j by the following table; every unlisted coefficient is zero:

    C76 = 2M40+7M31+9M22
    C75 = M50+13M41+31M32
    C74 = 5M51+32M42+52M33
    C73 = 10M52+38M43
    C72 = 10M53+22M44
    C71 = 5M54
    C70 = M55
    C66 = 2M50+16M41+33M32
    C65 = 13M51+70M42+112M33
    C64 = 32M52+117M43
    C63 = 38M53+85M44
    C62 = 22M54
    C61 = 5M55
    C56 = 9M51+39M42+56M33
    C55 = 39M52+132M43
    C54 = 66M53+141M44
    C53 = 48M54
    C52 = 12M55
    C46 = 15M52+41M43
    C45 = 52M53+109M44
    C44 = M63+59M54
    C43 = M64+22M55
    C36 = 11M53+19M44
    C35 = M63+37M54
    C34 = 3M64+23M55
    C33 = 2M65
    C26 = 3M54
    C25 = 3M64+15M55
    C24 = 3M65
    C23 = M66
    C15 = 3M65
    C14 = M66
    C05 = M66.

Direct substitution of (2)--(3), multiplication by the displayed positive denominator, and collection of the powers of p,q gives the exact identity

    27b_1b_2b_3-F(1-F)
      =N(p,q,r,s)/[(p+r)^2(p+s)^2(q+r)^2(q+s)^2 D^3]. (4)

The table is a complete coefficient certificate for (4), not a finite set of sampled evaluations. It has 100 positive monomials when expanded; in particular N>0 for p,q,r,s>0. This proves strict (1) at j=0. Interchanging p,q proves it at j=1. Reversing the chosen cap replaces F by 1-F and exchanges the positive and negative pairs; the same argument therefore proves it at j=2,3. All repeated positive or negative raw values remain in the proof.

## 2. Triangular sections and boundary incidences

Suppose the section cuts off a vertex cap at vertex h. Write eta_i in (0,1] for its three incident edge intercept ratios, i!=h. Choosing that cap gives

    F=product_(i!=h) eta_i,
    3b_i=eta_i (i!=h),  3b_h=3-sum_(i!=h)eta_i.

For j=h, the right side of (1) is F, which is strictly greater than F(1-F). For j!=h, divide the desired inequality by F>0. It becomes

    eta_j(1-product eta_i) <= sum (1-eta_i).

This follows from eta_j<=1 and the elementary product inequality

    1-product eta_i <= sum (1-eta_i),

proved by expanding 1-abc=(1-a)+a(1-b)+ab(1-c). This treats triangular sections containing vertices or an edge as well. Reversing the chosen side leaves F(1-F) unchanged.

For completeness any remaining through-vertex boundary of a strict-quadrilateral family is also obtained by a limit of proper planes. The section retains positive two-dimensional area. In a fixed coordinate chart transverse to its limiting normal, its bounded section indicators converge almost everywhere, since a convex polygon boundary has planar area zero. The chart Jacobians converge, so both section areas and first moments converge by dominated convergence. Thus b and F converge and (1) persists. No halfspace boundary has positive three-dimensional tetrahedral volume.

Sharpness is attained, not merely approached. For 0<z<1 take a section whose vertex-cap intercepts are (z,1,1). It contains the edge between the two intercept-one vertices and is a proper section. Its centroid coordinates, in an appropriate ordering, are

    b=((1-z)/3,z/3,1/3,1/3),  F=z.

For either of the last two vertex indices, 27 times the complementary centroid product is exactly z(1-z). Hence the factor 27 in (1) cannot be lowered.

## 3. Consequence for common-centroid probability support

If several actual section planes share centroid b, every corresponding cap probability P_i obeys

    P_i(1-P_i) <= C(b),
    C(b)=27 product of the three smallest coordinates of b. (5)

For strict quadrilaterals the inequalities are strict. In the unresolved unique-noncentral configuration b_h>1/3, C(b)=27 product_(j!=h)b_j. The already proved specified-captured-vertex product bound gives the additional strict lower bound F_i>C(b) for each h-oriented quadrilateral cap, because its other captured coordinate is central. Thus those actual probabilities satisfy both

    F_i>C(b),  F_i(1-F_i)<C(b).                     (6)

When C(b)<1/4, (5) excludes the closed middle probability interval between (1-sqrt(1-4C))/2 and (1+sqrt(1-4C))/2 for strict quadrilaterals. These restrictions are actual geometric consequences, not assertions about arbitrary laws. They do not alone establish the three-probability support frontier in `candidate 98dc66551a701077`; the common normal balance and the common centroid still carry information beyond (6).

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_tetrahedral_cap_variance_product_defect_transport.py` independently reconstructs (2)--(4), verifies the full polynomial identity and all coefficient signs, and checks the stated sharp boundary family exactly.
